title: Assessing Demographic Disparities in Suicide in a Majority-Minority Metropolis: The Case of Miami-Dade County
abstract: Suicide remains an important public health issue in the United States. Although there exists a sizable knowledge base regarding descriptive patterns and prevention/intervention efforts, there remains an important gap in the literature with respect to documenting the intersection of race, gender, and specific lethal mechanisms within high-density, majority-minority metropolitan regions over multiple decades. Longitudinal data spanning four decades from Miami-Dade County (MDC) Florida, a majority-minority subtropical metropolis, points to important demographic differences with respect to both suicide rates as well as suicide modality. Implications for future research and prevention efforts are highlighted.
